solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe encourage one to get groundbreaking single out

definitions.text: Maybe encourage one to get groundbreaking
definitions.note: a cryptic reading: hand someone a pick
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read playfully: handing someone a digging tool is one way to urge them to start breaking ground
second meaning: to choose carefully and personally

explanation.surface: A cheerleader urges somebody on to make a groundbreaking record and release it as a single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groundbreaking' looks like praise for a record and 'single' like a music release; the first half is literal digging, the second is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand-pick is to choose someone personally and carefully, which is exactly to select or single them out.

clue.text: Husband in Soviet Union a cavalryman once

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: the small word sits inside the larger unit named beside it

parts.note: the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband living in the Soviet Union served as a cavalryman in years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The containment reads in reverse order: 'in Soviet Union a' means A goes inside USSR, all after the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Hussars were light cavalry soldiers, originally Hungarian, a type of mounted trooper now largely historical.

clue.text: Other parent presumably also missing opera

parts.note: nor means 'and not either', adding one more thing that is absent
if one parent is Pa, the other one is presumably Ma

explanation.surface: A child notes that the other parent is also absent from the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works as 'neither Pa nor Ma': with Pa gone, the other parent, Ma, is missing too.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is an opera by Bellini, famous for the aria Casta diva.

clue.text: After quiz, family you could turn to late in the day?

definitions.text: you could turn to late in the day?
definitions.note: a cryptic description: the thing a coach turns into at midnight

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them for information
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: After a pub quiz, you might turn to your family late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cinderella, the fairy godmother's coach turns back into a pumpkin at midnight; the question mark flags that the 'you' is a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale Cinderella's coach was made from a gourd and reverts to it at the stroke of midnight, the very end of the day.

clue.text: Complicated for a technician, unleashing loud chemical process?

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled and intricate, so the letters are mixed up
unleashing lets something go free, so that letter is released from the group

parts.note: taken as written
f is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A technician in a lab is told a loud chemical process is too complicated to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is broad: a chain reaction is chemical or nuclear, and figuratively any cascade of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain reaction is a self-sustaining series of chemical or nuclear reactions, each step triggering the next.

clue.text: Greeting for which parent, sadly, is not going forward

indicators.note: whatever is not going forward is going backward, so the letters are read right to left

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
alas is an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.surface: A greeting that a parent sadly cannot get going with, as if stuck in some awkward family reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a respectful greeting in Muslim countries, a low bow with the hand to the forehead, from the Arabic for peace.

clue.text: Charity account artist set up for Greek department

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help given to those in need
ac is the abbreviation for account
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A charity sets up an account for an artist, intended for a Greek department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'department' sounds like a university or government office; Greece's administrative regions were called departments (nomoi).
explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia is a region in the central Peloponnese, formerly one of the prefectures, or departments, of Greece.

clue.text: I agree I must meet obligations to provide services

parts.note: amen expresses agreement, so be it
taken as written
ties are bonds that oblige you

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that they must honour obligations to provide services.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful facilities or services, such as shops, libraries or parks, available to a community.

clue.text: Game, if clumsy player turning up with girl, no good at golf

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor
Jo is a girl's name
ng is the abbreviation for no good
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A clumsy player turns up to a round of golf with a girlfriend and plays no good game at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests a sportsman, but a ham is an actor, a player on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jongg is a Chinese game for four players using tiles, so it is a game.

clue.text: That is awfully harmful for a footballer

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly and messily, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for 'that is' or 'namely'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone comments that a nasty tackle was awfully harmful for the player on the receiving end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That is' looks like a mere opener, but it is the abbreviation sc. Rugby is a form of football, so a rugby player counts as a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum half is the rugby player who feeds the ball into the scrum, and rugby football players are footballers.

clue.text: Conflict in another case slow-witted hosts scaled down

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so the short form sits inside the run of clue words
an abbreviation is a name scaled down, so the short letters are swapped for the full name

parts.note: three letters straddle the hyphen, slo-w-wi-tted, giving a lower-case abbreviation
turned into the other case, capitals, those three letters are the standard abbreviation for the 1914-18 war, written out in full

explanation.surface: A war breaks out among slow-witted hosts whose party has been cut back, unlike some other occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters are lower case in the clue; 'in another case' asks for them in capitals, WWI, the shortened form of the answer. 'Conflict' is the definition at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War of 1914 to 1918 was a global conflict, commonly abbreviated WWI.

clue.text: Commentator's staunch European

indicators.note: a commentator speaks to listeners, so the word is what we hear rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: to staunch a flow, of blood for example, is to check or stop it

explanation.surface: A sports commentator praises a loyal, staunch European player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staunch' reads as the adjective meaning loyal, but it is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A Czech is a native of the Czech Republic in central Europe, so a kind of European.

clue.text: American or Caribbean music covered by a network

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something covered by another thing sits wrapped inside it

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
ska is a Jamaican music style, forerunner of reggae

explanation.surface: A broadcaster weighs whether to cover American or Caribbean music on its network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American or Caribbean music' reads as a choice of two music genres; 'American' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alaskan comes from the US state of Alaska, so is an American.

clue.text: Switch to fiddle used by old composer

parts.note: a switch is a thin flexible rod or cane
to rig is to fiddle or manipulate dishonestly
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old composer swaps over to playing the fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a violin for a composer, but it means to cheat. Joaquin Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquin Rodrigo was a twentieth-century Spanish composer, famous for guitar works.

clue.text: Reducing money for American sailor after swindle

indicators.note: after tells us the pieces named before it are placed behind the piece named next, not in clue order

parts.note: a con is a confidence trick
a cent is a coin of US currency
a rating is a navy sailor without a commission

explanation.surface: An American sailor's pay is cut after he is caught in a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reducing money' reads as a pay cut; 'Reducing' alone is the definition, in the sense of boiling down a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry and cooking, concentrating a solution means reducing its volume by removing water.

clue.text: Cold homeless waif stops to see old war leader

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside the other word

parts.note: a chill is a coldness

indicators.note: homeless means without 'in', the crossword word for at home, so those letters are removed

parts.note: an urchin is a poor, ragged child

explanation.surface: A cold, homeless child stops someone in the street to see an old war leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homeless' is a real hardship in the surface; in the wordplay, home is IN, so the waif loses those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Winston Churchill was Britain's prime minister through the Second World War, a celebrated wartime leader.

clue.text: Poor black lad sold nuts

definitions.note: a noun here: nuts are cranks or eccentrics

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poor boy sells nuts at a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food a lad might sell, or an adjective meaning crazy; it is a plural noun for eccentric people.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddballs are eccentric or strange people, the same as nuts or cranks.

clue.text: Tricks pair at bridge — opponents there?

parts.note: a double is a pair, two of something
to bridge a gap is to cross it
in the card game bridge the players are North, South, East and West, and East and South are neighbours on opposing sides

explanation.surface: A pair of card players trick their opponents during a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' does double duty in the surface: the clue word is the crossing, and 'there' then refers back to bridge as the card game, whose players are named after compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross someone is to betray or cheat them, so double-crosses are tricks played on a trusting party.

clue.text: Sensationally, if clearly, making speed of light run!

indicators.note: making one thing into another changes it, so one letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: lucidly means clearly
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A physics headline breathlessly announces that the speed of light has been made to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Luridly means in a shocking, vivid way designed to sensationalise, as in lurid tabloid headlines.

clue.text: Car accessory that's fixed on for us

indicators.note: a fixed match or a fixed thing has been rigged or rearranged, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A car accessory that a garage has fitted for us.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunroof is a panel in a car's roof that opens to let in light and air, an optional extra feature.

clue.text: Three couples send rude message — and in French

parts.note: to sext is to send a sexually explicit text message
et is French for and

explanation.surface: Three couples exchange rude messages, some of them in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextet is a group of six, and three couples make six people.

clue.text: Rum sort of jacket seen on graduate

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree holder
a cardi is a cardigan, a knitted jacket

explanation.surface: Students remark on the odd jacket worn by a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective meaning odd, describing the jacket; it is the drink. In an across answer, 'on' puts the jacket after the graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a famous brand of white rum.

clue.text: Crescent, one French in character, largely

indicators.note: one item is placed in another, sitting inside it
largely means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a character is a letter of the alphabet
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A croissant-shaped crescent is one French character in a big way.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent-shaped or half-moon object or space, such as a semicircular window; the name means little moon.

clue.text: Letter: it's likely to arrive after Thursday

parts.note: Th is an abbreviation for Thursday
ETA is estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: A letter posted now is expected to arrive some time after Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the arrival piece behind the day's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Owner of estate left thoroughfare, accepting fine

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
Rd is the abbreviation for road
A1 means first-rate or fine, written here with the letter I for the digit 1

explanation.surface: A landowner abandons the road but agrees to pay a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty to be accepted; it is A1, excellent. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: Laird is the Scottish word for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Part of Hampshire town's free to redevelop

indicators.note: redeveloping a site rebuilds it in a new layout, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A town in Hampshire has been left free to redevelop itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest is a large area of heath and woodland, now a national park, in south-west Hampshire.

clue.text: Is spread betting clean? Yes, every so often!

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered on a horse at the start of a race

indicators.note: every so often means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A gambler asks if spread betting is honest and is told yes, at least now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread betting' looks like one financial term; the clue splits it so 'Is spread' is the definition. SP is the starting price in horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Splays is the third-person verb for spreads out or fans apart, so it swaps in for 'is spread' read actively as 'spreads'.

clue.text: Maybe gather tight trousers for director

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket something, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: taut means pulled tight
a ruff is a frilled collar made of gathered or pleated fabric, an example of a gather in dressmaking

explanation.surface: A tailor considers gathering in a pair of tight trousers for a film director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a garment but is a verb meaning pockets. Francois Truffaut was a French New Wave film director.
explanation.definitionFit: Francois Truffaut directed films such as The 400 Blows and Jules et Jim, so he is a director.
